title: WTF Ubuntu?
author: chalmovsky
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: 2026-11-02What the fuck, Ubuntu? In case you missed it: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical (CVSS 9.8) bug in the Linux kernel's TCP code. It's been there since 2016, so virtually every Linux server on the planet has it, and it can be hit remotely. Anthropic says it built a working exploit that gets root on a server. A total takeover. Debian patched it on October 16. Ubuntu still doesn't have a patch more than two weeks later. Every supported release, LTS included, is listed as "Vulnerable". Ubuntu's website promises "timely patches for critical vulnerabilities." Ubuntu hasn't shipped the patch nine days after it was rated 9.8 and six days after a working root exploit. Very fucking timely indeed. Software is full of this blabber where words mean nothing. Ubuntu uses words like these: "Timely." "Enterprise-grade." "Production grade." "Enterprise resilience. Developer velocity. Build with confidence on Ubuntu." Somebody, or perhaps worse, some special team at Canonical is dedicated to writing these........ So I'm asking again... What the fuck, Ubuntu? I'm moving all my servers off Ubuntu. I've completely lost trust in it. On the desktop I always hated it anyway. On servers I mostly used it because it's the default on most VPS providers, and I considered it the solid, no-drama LTS distro. Fuck that now. I can't express how crazy this is. I didn't have time to migrate my services and data when I learned about this, so I had to take all my servers that run Ubuntu offline. Oh and btw, distros run by volunteers (Debian, Arch, Alpine...) hve shipped the fix. Meanwhile Ubuntu, made by a company that sells security subscriptions, hasn't. This is true as of 2026-11-02 14:48 UTC.

comments.author: BoppreH
comments.textRawHtml:
Worse yet, the Ubuntu security incident page[0] lists "Ubuntu Priority: High" (as opposed to Critical, which would trigger an out-of-schedule patch). There's a "Why this priority?" link that simply says:

> Why is this CVE high priority?

> See ubuntu cvss score

That's it, we don't even get a period on this TBD of a sentence. It's followed by a generic link that explains what "Ubuntu Priority" is, but that page contradicts their choice. Note that it doesn't offer any mitigations either, and even the (horrendously unclear) description is copied from the NIST page, so there's no actual message from Ubuntu.

I already had a bad feeling the first time I saw "Get more security updates through Ubuntu Pro" on `apt upgrade`, this is now the kick I needed to move to a different distro.

[0] https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-98432#priority-reason

children.author: WesternStar
children.textRawHtml:
I don't think this is fair. They don't do a good job of pointing you at their rationale which is in their security score here[0]. I ultimately had to have claude translate the kernelese in to something my small brain could understand but this is a bug that could crash your system but is unlikely to expose your confidential system data to attackers or degrade data on the system. Especially given that the exploit can only be done if packets with IP options. IP options are commonly dropped or removed from packets on the open web. You not only need a vulnerable system but a vulnerable request path through the internet which you would only know by trying this attack which is very timing dependent with the SYN,Retransmitted SYN and Reset all happening very close together. A motivated attacker could probably do this on your network but over the internet ... It sounds unlikely.

children.author: BoppreH
children.textRawHtml:
> this is a bug that could crash your system but is unlikely to expose your confidential system data to attackers or degrade data on the system

Red Hat disagrees[0][1]. They might be parroting Anthropic, and Anthropic might be exagerating the impact (likely!), but that's the current consensus about the vulnerability. If Ubuntu disagrees, they should have said something and not pasted "Cvss 3 Severity Score 9.8 · Critical" at the top of the page.

> A motivated attacker could probably do this on your network

I find that's still catastrophic given how centralized cloud environments are.

children.author: BoppreH
children.textRawHtml:
That would still be an RCE in the default install under certain circumstances, and the security advisory has no legible description or mitigations for an issue that other vendors have patched two weeks ago.

I would be perfectly ok if they had either quietly patched it earlier (like Debian), or communicated their prioritization, or they inexplicably delayed it but provided a high quality advisory (like Red Hat).

I don't like complaining about my fellow security engineers, but this one was real bad and is still personally affecting me.

children.author: yusyusyus
children.textRawHtml:
TCP options are quite different from IP options.

IP options are annoying in big fast routers because they have to take the slow route via CPU. As there's not a lot of use in accepting packets (externally at least) with IP options, they tend to be dropped totally (but will almost certainly be policed aggressively to the CPU as the CPU is not good for moving many packets).

children.author: wtch98
children.textRawHtml:
> It sounds like iphones use mptcp in the wild, which use tcp options, so im not sure how true this is.

There's so much commentary misunderstanding what ip-options are that I find it difficult to make any judgement call. I do know that I've got routers on 5 continents with hundreds of public IPs and none have triggered an IP packet with an ip-option arriving on the WAN side, or seen on the internal side other than ones I've created with scapy trying to reproduce this. I also can't get these packets to traverse any internet paths I've tried.

children.author: tkinom
children.textRawHtml:
Asked claude/haiku5.5 to review that cve against my server, docker images. Claude had passwordless ssh access to that server and no root access. It did the review, confirm that server has the volubility, asked me to ran a few sudo commands, give it the output. It asked me to run a command to disable mptcp option.

I then asked it to do complete cve reviews on the host server (U 26.04 was installed a few weeks back) and docker images on that server and update the security review and added a task to do daily check on ubuntu website on kernel security update.

EDIT: Just asked claude if it can write a patch and build a image on top and fixed the issue on my server. It said it can. And point out that it can apply the 2 lines patches https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/e3f33b0.patch and build a kernel image on this issue for me. FYI....
children.textZhHtml:
要求 claude/haiku5.5 针对我的服务器、docker 镜像审查该 cve。 Claude 可以通过无密码 ssh 访问该服务器，但没有 root 访问权限。 它进行了审查，确认服务器具有流畅性，要求我运行一些 sudo 命令，并给出输出。 它要求我运行一个命令来禁用 mptcp 选项。

然后我要求它在主机服务器（几周前安装了 U 26.04）和该服务器上的 docker 映像上进行完整的 cve 审查，并更新安全审查，并添加了一项任务来在 ubuntu 网站上进行内核安全更新的日常检查。

编辑：只是询问 claude 是否可以编写补丁并在其上构建映像并修复我的服务器上的问题。 据说可以。 并指出它可以应用 2 行补丁 https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/e3f33b0.patch 并为我构建有关此问题的内核映像。 仅供参考....

children.author: voakbasda
children.textRawHtml:
Yeah, their lack of a satisfactory response is the final nail in their coffin. This incident escalates my consulting advice about Ubuntu from “not recommended” to “switch immediately”.

Some of my clients may be surprised by this change, as I once advocated for Ubuntu as a good choice for a development and deployment platform. While that has not been true for quite a while, they have now jumped the shark into eel-infested waters; I cannot take them seriously any longer.

children.author: thayne
children.textRawHtml:
Not always. Notably, if you have compliance requirements like needing FIPS encryption (say because you have government customers), or that requires you to use a commercial vendor, debian won't work. And if you need more up to date system packages, or a reliable release cadence, Ubuntu might be better.

On desktop, if you need proprietary drivers, Ubuntu is easier to set up.

But yes, if debian works for you, I wouldn't use Ubuntu.
